events.description: UN Monitoring Team releases its six-monthly report on al-Qaeda and ISIS; omits Saif al-Adel's presence in Iran
US kills senior ISIS leader Abu Khadija
Zawahiri killed about three years before recording; al-Qaeda has not announced his death or successor
Large-scale IS Somalia attack on a Puntland base conducted by foreign (Arab and Tanzanian) fighters
Puntland offensive against IS Somalia; claims 200 killed and 150 arrested; no senior leaders killed; US captured finance emir and killed an Omani external attack planner
al-Shabaab gains in Lower Shabelle beginning December 2024
Senior al-Shabaab leader Mohamed Mire killed late 2024
Abbey Gate suicide bombing in Kabul partly financed by IS Somalia/al-Karrar office money
Hamas attack on Israel, reflected since in ISIS and al-Qaeda propaganda
Islamic State emerges in Somalia and faces intense al-Shabaab purges
US seeks to ease sanctions on Syria's interim regime under Sharaa

key_claims: The UN report ducks Saif al-Adel's presence in Iran, a sign of no member-state consensus; Fitton-Brown argues the omission undermines the report's 'weak al-Qaeda leadership' framing.
Al-Qaeda is gradually being incorporated into the Iran-led axis of resistance; Houthi–al-Shabaab ties are an example.
No al-Qaeda affiliate has split despite three years of Saif al-Adel leading from Iran; JNIM split rumors are undercut by AQIM's sway over its leadership.
The ISIS caliph is widely believed to be Abdulqadir Mumin of IS Somalia, but unconfirmed; ISIS obscures its leadership.
ISKP (al-Siddiq office) remains the most immediate kinetic threat to the West; ISWAP may exceed 10,000 fighters; IS Somalia (600-800, half foreign) is key to ISIS finances and helped fund Abbey Gate.
UN fighter estimates are consensus floors, not literal counts; the trend matters more; al-Qaeda in Afghanistan was long understated at 50-100.
HTS dominates Syria and Iranian militias dominate Iraq; ISIS (~3,000 in Syria) is waiting for either to fail.
Hurras al-Din retains ~2,000 fighters; hosts doubt the report's 'no active ties' between HTS and al-Qaeda.
